$1$ intersects the $x$-axis.

The intersection is $(${{field-1}}$,$ {{field-2}}$)$. Give exact values."] [:db/add "cdd2a20d-8d5c-5e49-82a4-60608d28d3c9" :question/worked-solution "First find the point on the curve.

$$
f(1)=-4\sqrt{(1)}+3(1)+2=1.
$$

The normal passes through $(1,1)$.

Rewrite the radical or reciprocal using powers, then differentiate.

$$
\begin{aligned}
f(x)&=- 4 x^{\frac{1}{2}} + 3 x + 2, \\f'(x)&=3 - \frac{2}{x^{\frac{1}{2}}}=3 - \frac{2}{\sqrt{x}}.
\end{aligned}
$$

Evaluate the tangent slope and take its negative reciprocal to find the normal slope.

$$
\begin{aligned}
m_t=f'(1)&=3 - \frac{2}{\sqrt{(1)}}=1, \\m_n=-\frac{1}{m_t}&=-\frac{1}{(1)}=-1.
\end{aligned}
$$

Use point-slope form through $(1,1)$.

$$
\begin{aligned}
y-(1)&=-1(x-(1)), \\y&=- x + 2.
\end{aligned}
$$

At the $x$-axis, $y=0$.

$$
\begin{aligned}
0&=-1x+(2), \\x&=2.
\end{aligned}
$$

The intersection is $(2,0)$."] [:db/add "cdd2a20d-8d5c-5e49-82a4-60608d28d3c9" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/hard] [:db/add "cdd2a20d-8d5c-5e49-82a4-60608d28d3c9" :question/answer-fields $$
\begin{aligned}
